name: Stormwind City
summary: White-walled Stormwind is the greatest haven of men, and the heart of the Alliance. Yet its king is lost. The crown now rests on a boy of ten.

sections.title: Rise from the Ashes
sections.body:
Stormwind is old. More than a thousand years ago, the descendants of the Arathi founded it. For long generations it flourished, a realm that needed no one's help. Then the Horde came through the Dark Portal. The southern continent was laid waste, and in the First War the city was razed.

Its survivors followed Sir Anduin Lothar north, across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. When the Horde fell in the Second War, King Terenas Menethil II and the Alliance paid for Stormwind to rise again. The Stonemasons Guild raised it anew in polished white stone, with canals running through its boroughs.

sections.title: A Divided Court
sections.body:
But the white stone hides a troubled house. The House of Nobles quarreled with the Stonemasons Guild over wages, and the quarrel left the kingdom crippled by debt. The guild's workers rose in riot. They were driven from the very city they had built.

Then King Varian Wrynn vanished on his way to a summit. Lest panic spread, the crown passed to his son Prince Anduin Wrynn. He is ten years old. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon rules now as Regent and commander of the army. And at his side stands the royal advisor, Lady Katrana Prestor.

sections.title: Heart of the Grand Alliance
sections.body: With Lordaeron overrun by the Scourge, men look to Stormwind above every other city. The faithful gather at the Cathedral of Light. And in the Valley of Heroes, tall statues honor the Sons of Lothar. They passed beyond the Dark Portal, and were seen no more.

sections.title: Where the Masons Went
sections.body: The stonemasons gathered again in Westfall under their guildmaster, Edwin VanCleef. There they became the Defias Brotherhood, red-masked bandits now strangling the kingdom’s farmland. The builders of Stormwind’s white walls have sworn to make the House of Nobles pay for every stone.

sections.title: A Friend at Court
sections.body: The Defias Brotherhood found help within Stormwind Keep. Lord Gregor Lescovar of the House of Nobles secretly dealt with the Brotherhood, passing along the kingdom’s plans while sitting among the lords who had cheated the stonemasons.

sections.title: Shadows in the Keep
sections.body: Lady Katrana Prestor has secretly guided the House of Nobles’ decisions. She inflamed its conflict with the stonemasons and ignored pleas for military aid from settlements such as Westfall and Redridge. She also whispered poison to Highlord Bolvar, keeping Stormwind’s legions idle and divided as unrest beyond the city walls threatens the throne.

faq.answer: Ten-year-old Prince Anduin Wrynn holds Stormwind’s crown, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs as Regent and commands its military. Bolvar relies on royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor’s counsel as King Varian Wrynn remains missing.

faq.q: What happened to King Varian Wrynn?
faq.answer: King Varian vanished under suspicious circumstances while sailing to a diplomatic summit in Theramore. His disappearance was kept quiet to preserve stability, though rumors spread through the streets and countryside.

faq.q: Why was the city rebuilt, and by whom?
faq.answer: The Orcish Horde burned the original city to the ground during the First War. After the Second War, the Alliance of Lordaeron funded the rebuilding, and master craftsman Edwin VanCleef led the Stonemasons Guild in raising the capital from white stone.

faq.q: Why did the stonemasons rebel against the crown?
faq.answer: The House of Nobles took on heavy debts while expanding Stormwind’s military, then refused to pay the Stonemasons Guild its promised wages. When Edwin VanCleef demanded payment, the nobles disbanded the guild. The workers rioted and were driven from the city.

faq.q: Who are the giant statues in the Valley of Heroes?
faq.answer: The Valley of Heroes honors the Sons of Lothar: General Turalyon, Ranger Captain Alleria Windrunner, Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, and Danath Trollbane. The statues commemorate the heroes who entered the Dark Portal to Draenor to seal the rift and protect Azeroth.

faq.q: How does Stormwind connect to Ironforge?
faq.answer: The Deeprun Tram, an underground railway, connects Stormwind to Ironforge. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque built it at King Magni Bronzebeard’s request, so the capitals could trade swiftly and reinforce one another in war.

faq.q: Why isn't Stormwind sending troops to help Westfall and Redridge?
faq.answer: The royal court, guided by Lady Katrana Prestor, says Stormwind cannot spare troops from its walls and nearby borders. Kingdom finances are strained, and political infighting has paralyzed the House of Nobles, leaving regional towns to depend on their local militias.

angles.text: As a human, Stormwind is your people’s last great seat of sovereign power after Lordaeron, Alterac, and Dalaran fell in the north.
As an Alliance member, you can look to Stormwind for naval might, spiritual grounding, and vital diplomatic leadership. It is the Grand Alliance’s most populous metropolis.
As a paladin, you can find the Cathedral of Light, the south’s chief sanctuary of your faith. It trains knights of the Silver Hand and upholds justice.
As a rogue, you can find SI:7’s headquarters beneath Old Town’s stone streets. It runs the Alliance’s chief intelligence and espionage network.
As a dwarf, you can travel the Deeprun Tram to your kin in the Dwarven District. They maintain close trade and military ties with the human kingdom.
